title: Open flat models and the compact-support Tor window
statement: Fix a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ and a prime $\ell\ne p$. Let $U,W,V$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and let $U\xrightarrow j W\xrightarrow r V$ be $k$-morphisms, with $j$ an open immersion and $r$ proper [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $R$ be any finite commutative ring annihilated by a power of $\ell$. Use the ordinary small-etale constant-ring module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], constructibility [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf], and Tor amplitude [def-kun-tor-amplitude]. For integers $a\le b$, let $K$ be bounded constructible of Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ on $U$, and let $P$ be any representing cochain complex of flat constructible $R_U$-modules, zero outside $[a,b]$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Termwise extension by zero $j_!P$ [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero] represents $Dj_!K$, has flat constructible terms, is zero outside $[a,b]$, and is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Thus $Dj_!K$ is bounded constructible of Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$. There exists an integer $e\ge0$ depending only on $r$ such that every geometric fibre has torsion etale cohomology zero in degrees greater than $2e$, and for every $R,a,b,K,P$ as above, $Rr_*Dj_!K$ is bounded constructible of Tor amplitude in $[a,b+2e]$. Here $Rr_*Dj_!$ is the ordinary compactification functor of [def-amb-etale-compact-support].

proof.text: Quasi-compactness of V follows from its quasi-compact structure morphism to Spec k. Apply lem-sfb-finite-proper-geometric-cd-bound to r and retain its nonnegative e and torsion cohomology clause. Convert F.IsTorsion to its colimit characterization with lem-weil-pbc-torsion-sheaf-characterizations. Algebraically closed fields are separably closed. An integer i>2e is nonnegative, hence i=Int.toNat(i); the natural-degree vanishing gives exactly the required integer-degree bound, before any coefficient or input choices.

source.place: Tags 0A3V, 00P3, 0F0V and 03QU, via the uniform geometric-fibre bound; local torsion as in the blueprint sk-def-pbc

proof.text: Let J=j_! and E=J(P). Exactness of J and mapDerivedCategoryFactors identify Q(E) with D(J)(Q(P)), then the given isomorphism Q(P)~=K identifies it with D(J)(K). An additive functor sends zero objects to zero, so E retains the support [a,b].

source.place: Tag 03DJ, lemma-extension-by-zero-exact; localization of an exact functor

proof.text: Use the open-extension flatness clause of lem-sfb-open-closed-flatness, proved in the adopted source as flat_openImmersionLowerShriek_obj. The open restriction is the input by the adjunction unit; the closed-complement restriction is zero. Every geometric point factors through the open or the closed complement, so the geometric-fibre flatness criterion gives flatness of j_!P^q. The braiding transports the assumed exact tensorRight(P^q) to exact tensorLeft(P^q), giving the source flat predicate and returning its right tensor clause for E.

W is locally Noetherian by finite type over k, hence the open immersion j is quasi-compact. Convert finite-value constructibility to source constructibility by lem-weil-pbc-constructible-etale-module-sheaf-comparison; apply lem-fin-extension-by-zero and convert back. This gives constructible terms. The exact-functor derived homology isomorphism H^q(K) followed by J ~= H^q(D(J)(K)) transports constructibility and all cohomology vanishing bounds from the given bounded constructibility of K. Thus D(J)(K) is bounded constructible; constructibility of cohomology is not deduced from constructibility of terms.

source.place: Constructible extension by zero along a quasi-compact open; exact functors commute with homology

proof.text: The complex E has flat terms and vanishes outside [a,b]. CochainComplex.isStrictlyGE_iff and isStrictlyLE_iff give its strict degree bounds. The source bounded-flat criterion CochainComplex.kFlat_of_bounded_of_flat proves K-flatness in the exact monoidal category used by the statement. Apply lem-kun-flat-bounded-tor-amplitude, transport along Q(E)~=D(J)(K), and use DerivedCategory.hasTorAmplitudeIn_iff_torAmplitudeIn to obtain the required etale Tor interval [a,b].

source.place: Tag 06YQ; bounded flat Tor-amplitude implication, Tag 08G1

proof.text: For the fibre hypothesis of det-ctf-finite-proper-tor, every section killed by ell^n has finite additive order since ell>0. Such a sectionwise torsion sheaf is locally torsion, so Step 1 gives the IsZero cohomology bound with d=2e. Apply the proper finite-Tor theorem to r, R, and D(J)(K), using bounded constructibility from Step 4 and Tor amplitude from Step 5. Simplifying the natural-to-integer cast of 2e gives [a,b+2e]. The theorem uses the unbounded rightDerivedLowerStar itself, which is the proper factor in def-amb-etale-compact-support; no bounded-below comparison or change of coefficient category is needed.
